title: Pseudocode — DK Bond Tracker (37 atomic functions)
sources: docs/SRS_DK_Bond_Tracker_v1.json (Status Engine Rules D5 and acceptance criteria)
docs/Feasibility_XLSM_Parser_v1.json (import specifics: sheet trim, header-derived grid, K/L recompute, L1 reconciliation)
d5_rule: Danger = ANY unpaid past month (not just previous month); Completed overrides Danger when months paid >= tenure; zero-value = unpaid preserved

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: database file path
OUTPUT: SQLite file with bonds, payment_ledger (UNIQUE(bond_id, month)) and home_plan tables
ERRORS: unwritable project folder or schema creation failure -> raise named error ERR-schema-create and surface via AF-30; never swallow
1. If the file already exists and all three tables are present, return the handle unchanged (idempotent, no destructive re-create).
2. Create or open the SQLite file at the given path inside the project folder.
3. CREATE TABLE bonds with stable schema keys: id, isin UNIQUE, company, rating, principle_tl, tenure_months, maturity_date, maturity_amount, purchase_date, broker, interest_start_month, payment_type, discount.
4. CREATE TABLE payment_ledger with id, bond_id referencing bonds, month TEXT in YYYY-MM form, amount REAL, paid INTEGER, and a UNIQUE(bond_id, month) constraint.
5. CREATE TABLE home_plan with month_index PRIMARY KEY, saving, rate, per_year_interest, countdown, remaining_interest plus schedule total fields.
6. CREATE INDEX on payment_ledger(bond_id, month) for status scans.
7. Post-check: assert no column name anywhere in the schema matches a month token (no per-month columns ever exist — D3, months are rows only).
8. Any failure at any step aborts with the named error; partial schema creation is rolled back and reported, never left half-built.
entries.complexity_note: single DDL transaction (schema is static)
edge_cases: database file exists but one table is missing -> create missing tables idempotently, do not drop data
project folder read-only -> named ERR-schema-create surfaced visibly
legacy database containing month-like columns -> post-check fails and reports the D3 violation

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: path to source XLSM
OUTPUT: normalized workbook handle with trimmed sheet-name lookup; source file SHA-256 and mtime recorded
ERRORS: file missing, unreadable, not a valid XLSM, or openpyxl unavailable -> raise named error ERR-workbook-open naming the operation; surface via AF-30, no silent empty result
1. Check the source path exists and is readable; abort with a named error if not.
2. Compute the source file SHA-256 and record its mtime before opening (FR-08 evidence that the file stays unmodified).
3. Load pass 1 with openpyxl data_only=True to obtain cached values.
4. Load pass 2 with openpyxl data_only=False to obtain formulas.
5. Both loads open the file read-only; the file is never written, saved or closed for writing.
6. Build a normalized sheet lookup: for every sheet name, strip leading and trailing whitespace as the lookup key (the watch-list sheet is stored as 'Bond - Watch list ' with a trailing space).
7. All later sheet access goes through the normalized lookup, never raw exact-string matching.
8. Re-verify SHA-256 and mtime after the run unchanged; a changed hash aborts with a named error instead of being ignored.
entries.complexity_note: two sequential file reads, O(file size)
edge_cases: sheet name carries trailing/leading spaces -> found via trimmed key
file replaced between open and close -> hash mismatch aborts with named error
cached values absent in data_only pass -> dependent extracts report missing-cache errors, they do not default to 0

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: normalized workbook handle
OUTPUT: list of 15 bond master records (isin, company, rating, principle_tl, tenure_months, maturity_date, maturity_amount, purchase_date, broker, interest_start_month, payment_type)
ERRORS: Monthly Returns sheet absent, header keywords undetectable, or a bond row missing a required field -> raise named error ERR-extract-masters listing the field and row; surface via AF-30
1. Locate the Monthly Returns sheet through the normalized (trimmed) name lookup.
2. Scan row 1 for bond columns by header keyword (Company Name, ISN, Status, Tenure, Interest Starting Month, Purchase Date, Rating, Principle TL Amount, Maturity Amount, Maturity Date, Broker, Payment Type) — never by fixed column position.
3. Take company names from column E where the header keyword resolves there; column A is Status and column B is Purchase Date and are read only via their own keywords.
4. Walk bond rows from row 2 downward until the name/ISIN column is empty; extract exactly 15 records.
5. Copy every field verbatim into stable schema keys; no header string is stored as a key (FR-23).
6. If any required field is empty or non-parseable, abort with a named error naming the field and row; never fill a default silently.
entries.complexity_note: single pass over header row and 15 bond rows
edge_cases: header text renamed or misspelled (e.g. Staus) -> keyword detection still resolves by schema key, display rename changes nothing
fewer or more than 15 bond rows -> count reported, mismatch flagged to validation (AF-07)
duplicate ISIN in extraction -> detected downstream by AF-07/AF-28, not silently deduplicated here

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: normalized workbook handle, bond column mapping from AF-03
OUTPUT: list of payment records (bond isin, month YYYY-MM, amount, paid flag); per-bond recomputed K (Till Return) and L (Balance) as parse evidence
ERRORS: row-1 headers unparseable, month grid empty, or non-numeric amount in a month cell -> raise named error ERR-extract-grid with sheet/row/column context; surface via AF-30
1. Scan row 1 from the first month-header column rightward (feasibility: cols 14..96) and parse every date or mmm-yy header into a YYYY-MM month key — the grid extent is derived at runtime, no hardcoded month list (the real window is 83 headers, 2025-09..2032-07).
2. Stop the grid at the first run of empty headers; never assume a fixed last column and never hardcode Sep-2025..Feb-2027.
3. For each bond row and each derived month column, emit one payment record (isin, month, amount, paid flag); an empty cell emits an unpaid record, a zero cell keeps amount 0 with paid false (zero = unpaid per D5).
4. Recompute K for the bond as the sum of its month-row cells (the workbook K is =SUM(Nn:XFDn), a formula, not a stored number).
5. Recompute L for the bond as K minus J (maturity amount), matching the workbook formula =Kn-Jn; the static J is read verbatim.
6. Store recomputed K and L as parse evidence only; dashboard cached cells are evidence, never truth (NFR-7 live recompute).
7. Non-numeric or accounting-formatted cell values are converted explicitly; anything unconvertible aborts with a named error rather than defaulting to 0.
entries.complexity_note: O(bonds x derived months) cell scan (15 x 83)
edge_cases: grid wider than expected (83 headers, cols 14..96 plus 4 empty trailing cells) -> extent stops at first empty header
simulated month beyond Feb-2027 -> still derived from headers, no window clamp
K/L read as static cells -> forbidden; always recompute, cached values used only as cross-check evidence
zero amount cell -> preserved as amount 0, paid false, never dropped

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: normalized workbook handle
OUTPUT: list of 84 home_plan records (month_index, saving, rate, per_year_interest, countdown, remaining_interest) plus schedule totals
ERRORS: Home Plan sheet absent, fewer than 84 schedule rows, or unparseable cell -> raise named error ERR-extract-homeplan with row context; surface via AF-30, never a partial schedule presented as complete
1. Locate the Home Plan sheet through the normalized (trimmed) name lookup.
2. Walk month index 1..84 and read the static columns (date, month index, saving, rate, countdown) verbatim from the values pass.
3. Read formula cells (per-year interest = C*D, remaining interest, schedule totals) from the data_only cached values; if a cache is missing, report a named error instead of substituting 0.
4. Preserve irregular savings exactly at their original month positions: 39588, 10063 and 0 must appear where the workbook puts them (ERR-06 verbatim preservation).
5. Read the trailing Per Month / Per Year / TL summary rows as static totals.
6. Verify the extracted row count is exactly 84; a shortfall aborts with a named error.
entries.complexity_note: single pass over 84 schedule rows
edge_cases: irregular savings 39588, 10063, 0 -> verbatim in original positions, never normalized or filled
saving value 0 is a real value, not a missing value -> stored as 0
formula cell without cached value -> named ERR-extract-homeplan, no silent default

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: normalized workbook handle
OUTPUT: list of watch-list input records (isin, face value, principle, T.L.P, discount inputs)
ERRORS: watch-list sheet not found under trimmed lookup, or a bond row missing inputs -> raise named error ERR-extract-watchlist naming the row; surface via AF-30
1. Resolve the sheet through the normalized name lookup so 'Bond - Watch list ' (trailing space) is found by its trimmed key.
2. Detect input columns by header keyword, not fixed positions (face value, principle, T.L.P, discount inputs).
3. Walk every bond row on the sheet and extract the inputs verbatim into stable schema keys.
4. Report rows present on the sheet but with no matching bond ISIN as named warnings in the extraction result; do not drop them silently.
5. Abort with a named error if the sheet is missing entirely or contains no bond rows.
entries.complexity_note: single pass over watch-list rows
edge_cases: sheet name with trailing space -> matched via trimmed key, no exact-string coupling
formula cells in analytics columns -> inputs only; analytics are computed later by AF-32
watch-list row for unknown ISIN -> surfaced as explicit warning, not discarded

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: extracted bond masters (AF-03), payment records (AF-04), home plan records (AF-05), watch list inputs (AF-06)
OUTPUT: validation result — pass, or an explicit list of named failures
ERRORS: any check failure -> collect named errors (ERR-04 duplicate ISIN, ERR-05 incomplete import) and abort the import; never present a partial import as success (FR-21)
1. Collect the full bond set from AF-03 and run the full-set duplicate-ISIN check (AF-28); every occurrence of a duplicated ISIN is listed with its rows (ERR-04).
2. Check completeness of master fields: each of the 15 bonds must carry every required field; list each missing field by name and row.
3. Check payment coverage: every bond has records across its entire derived month grid; report gaps by (isin, month).
4. Check home plan completeness: exactly 84 rows present with month_index 1..84 contiguous.
5. Check watch-list inputs present for every bond row.
6. If any check failed, assemble the failure list and abort the pipeline with ERR-05 — the import stops before any write (AF-09) and the failures are printed for the operator.
7. Never downgrade a failure to a warning and continue; silent skipping of rows is forbidden (ERR-01).
entries.complexity_note: O(n) over bonds, ledger rows and schedule rows
edge_cases: same ISIN on row 2 and row 40 of 40 bonds -> both occurrences flagged
bond with empty tenure or start month -> named completeness failure, import aborts
zero payment rows for a future-start bond -> grid derived from headers still expects the months; gap reported

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: bond masters (AF-03), payment records with recomputed K/L (AF-04), baseline figures (PRD/SRS exit figures and workbook-derived figures, ADR-10)
OUTPUT: reconciliation report of computed vs baseline with deltas; explicit L1 flag when figures do not match the OPEN baseline
ERRORS: any mismatch against the baseline -> report the mismatch and flag L1 OPEN, then abort or hold the import as flagged; force-matching, adjusting computed figures to the baseline, or silently passing is forbidden (FR-09, ADR-10)
1. Compute from extracted data: bond count, Total Investment = SUM(principle_tl) over all bonds, Total Till Return = recomputed SUM(K) across bonds, Total Balance = recomputed SUM(L) across bonds.
2. Load the baseline candidates: PRD/SRS exit figures (Total Till Return 111638.57, Total Balance -925503.44) and the workbook-derived figures (56227.88, -1165738.34), with bond count 15 and Total Investment 1037142.01.
3. Print computed and baseline figures side by side with signed deltas for every measure.
4. For each measure, compare against the chosen baseline with a zero tolerance for the OPEN baseline; a non-zero delta is a mismatch.
5. On ANY mismatch: emit an explicit L1 reconciliation flag (status OPEN per ADR-10) carrying both numbers and the delta, and abort-or-flag the pipeline step — the mismatch is reported, never silently reconciled and never passed.
6. Record that the Balance definition itself is contested (workbook L = K - J maturity amount vs PRD Balance = Till Return - Total Investment) as part of the L1 flag; the flag names both sub-decisions as OPEN owner decisions.
7. No acceptance result may be declared green against stale PRD numbers; re-baselining is the owner's action, the code only reports.
entries.complexity_note: single query pass over extracted records plus four baseline comparisons
edge_cases: Total Till Return computed 56227.88 vs baseline 111638.57 -> L1 flagged OPEN, import held, never force-matched
Total Balance definition conflict (K-J vs Till Return - Investment) -> reported inside the L1 flag, not silently resolved
bond count or Total Investment mismatch -> same report-and-abort path
baseline itself missing -> named error ERR-reconcile-baseline, not a skip

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: validated bond records (AF-03), payment records (AF-04), home plan records (AF-05), watch list inputs (AF-06), reconciliation result with L1 flag (AF-08)
OUTPUT: populated bonds, payment_ledger and home_plan tables; import report with imported counts, reconciliation summary and the L1 flag
ERRORS: any write failure or constraint violation -> roll back the whole transaction and raise named ERR-commit-import; a partial import is never committed or reported as success (ERR-05)
1. Preconditions: schema exists (AF-01), validation passed (AF-07), reconciliation report produced (AF-08).
2. Begin one explicit SQLite transaction.
3. Insert exactly 15 bonds rows with master fields verbatim; UNIQUE(isin) violation aborts the transaction with a named error.
4. Insert one payment_ledger row per imported month cell; rely on UNIQUE(bond_id, month) and abort on violation instead of upserting silently.
5. Insert all 84 home_plan rows verbatim, including irregular savings values.
6. Store watch-list inputs with their bonds.
7. Commit once; on any failure roll back everything and raise the named error — no partial silent import.
8. After commit, re-verify the source XLSM SHA-256 and mtime unchanged (FR-08).
9. Emit the import report: counts per table plus the reconciliation summary, carrying the L1 flag verbatim — the flag is included in the report, never dropped.
entries.complexity_note: single transaction, O(records) inserts
edge_cases: duplicate ISIN during insert -> transaction rollback, named error
disk full or constraint failure mid-insert -> rollback leaves prior data intact
reconciliation L1 OPEN -> report still carries the flag; the flag is never swallowed by a successful commit

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: bond id, month (YYYY-MM), amount, paid flag
OUTPUT: exactly one new payment_ledger row
ERRORS: bond not found, month unparseable, amount non-numeric, or UNIQUE(bond_id, month) violation -> raise named error ERR-ledger-insert listing the failing field; surface via AF-30 (FR-21)
1. Verify the schema exists (AF-01) and the bond id resolves in bonds.
2. Validate month parses to YYYY-MM and amount is numeric; a zero amount is accepted as a real value (zero = unpaid per D5).
3. INSERT one payment_ledger row with the given bond ref, month, amount and paid flag.
4. If a row already exists for (bond_id, month), raise the named conflict error and direct the caller to the correction path (AF-11) — never silently overwrite.
5. Confirm exactly one row was written; never add a column to any table (D3).
entries.complexity_note: single row insert (single query)
edge_cases: duplicate (bond_id, month) insert -> named conflict error, no overwrite
amount 0 -> stored as 0 with paid flag false, counts as unpaid
future month beyond current date -> accepted; due/paid rendering decided at view time

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: ledger row id or (bond_id, month); new amount and/or paid flag, or a void instruction
OUTPUT: the updated or removed payment_ledger row
ERRORS: target row not found, invalid amount, or update affecting zero rows -> raise named error ERR-ledger-edit with the (bond_id, month) context; surface via AF-30
1. Resolve the target row by id or by (bond_id, month); if absent, raise the named not-found error.
2. On a correction: UPDATE amount and/or paid flag in place; the row keeps its identity.
3. On a void that must preserve the audit trail: set amount to 0 and paid flag to false — this row counts as unpaid everywhere (ERR-02, zero = unpaid per D5).
4. On a hard removal instruction: DELETE the single row; absence of a row also counts as unpaid.
5. Validate the final row state (numeric amount, parseable month); reject invalid updates with a named error rather than coercing.
6. Confirm exactly one row was changed; a change count of 0 raises the named error instead of succeeding silently.
entries.complexity_note: single row update or delete
edge_cases: correct amount to 0 -> row kept with amount 0, status engine treats it as unpaid
flip paid flag from true to false on an older past month -> next status read recomputes (AF-15)
deleting a row -> month becomes unpaid (no row), same D5 outcome
edit targets a non-existent month -> named not-found error, not a silent no-op

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: bond id, payment_ledger rows for that bond
OUTPUT: months paid count, Till Return (sum of paid ledger rows)
ERRORS: schema missing or ledger query failure -> raise named error ERR-query-totals; surface via AF-30, never return a silent 0 on failure
1. SELECT all payment_ledger rows for the bond id ordered by month.
2. months_paid = count of rows where paid flag is true AND amount > 0 (zero amount counts as unpaid per D5).
3. till_return = sum of amount over rows that count as paid.
4. If the bond has no rows, return months_paid = 0 and till_return = 0 as a legitimate empty result for a bond with no history (the query itself succeeded).
5. Return both figures; do not read or write any persisted Till Return column (query-only, DATA-05).
entries.complexity_note: single query over one bond's ledger rows
edge_cases: row with amount 0 -> excluded from months_paid and from Till Return
bond with no ledger rows -> legitimate 0/0 result, not an error
ledger query error -> named error surfaced, never a default 0 presented as data (ERR-03)

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: bonds table, payment_ledger table
OUTPUT: Total Investment, Total Till Return, Total Balance (Till Return - Maturity Amount)
ERRORS: query failure -> raise named error ERR-query-portfolio; surface via AF-30, never a silent 0 on failure
1. total_investment = SUM(bonds.principle_tl) over all bond rows (workbook column G equivalent).
2. total_till_return = SUM(payment_ledger.amount) over rows whose paid flag is true and amount > 0.
3. total_maturity_amount = SUM(bonds.maturity_amount).
4. total_balance = total_till_return - total_maturity_amount (workbook L = K - J definition).
5. Return the three figures as query results only; no stored total column is read or written (DATA-05).
6. If any underlying query raises, the named error propagates to AF-30; a zero result is only returned when the tables are genuinely empty.
entries.complexity_note: three aggregate queries, single query class
edge_cases: empty portfolio -> genuine zeros, query succeeded
zero-amount ledger rows -> excluded from Till Return (zero = unpaid)
Balance definition note: this function uses the workbook L = K - J rule; the ADR-10 contested definition is reported by AF-08, not silently swapped here

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: bond id, bond metadata (interest_start_month, tenure_months), payment_ledger rows for the bond, current month
INPUT ASSERTION (D5 applied exactly, verbatim rule): Danger = ANY unpaid past month (not just previous month); Completed overrides Danger when months paid >= tenure; zero-value = unpaid preserved
OUTPUT: status string — Danger | On-going | Completed
ERRORS: missing bond metadata or ledger query failure -> raise named error ERR-status-compute naming the bond; surface via AF-30, never a silent default status
1. Read bond metadata: start = interest_start_month (YYYY-MM), tenure = tenure_months; if either is missing or unparseable, raise the named error.
2. Build the due window: months from start through min(current month, start + tenure - 1); future months are never scanned.
3. For each past month in the window, classify as paid ONLY when a ledger row exists with paid flag true AND amount > 0; no row, paid flag false, or amount 0 all classify as unpaid (zero = unpaid preserved).
4. months_paid = count of paid months in the whole tenure; any_unpaid_past = at least one unpaid month in the past due window.
5. If months_paid >= tenure, return Completed — Completed overrides Danger even when historical gaps exist.
6. Else if any_unpaid_past is true, return Danger — this covers ANY unpaid past month, not just the previous month (an old miss with a paid previous month still reads Danger).
7. Else return On-going.
8. No scan-window limit: a bond whose window starts Feb-2031 or later is evaluated by the same rules (FR-19); the status is returned, never persisted to a status column.
entries.complexity_note: O(tenure) scan per bond, single query class
edge_cases: old past month unpaid but previous month paid -> Danger (not On-going)
months paid >= tenure with historical gaps -> Completed overrides Danger
row with amount 0 in a past month -> counts as unpaid, contributes to Danger
bond starting Feb-2031 or later -> same rules, no scan-window clamp (ERR-01)
no past due months yet (start in the future) and not full tenure -> On-going

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: bond id, updated ledger rows, current month
INPUT ASSERTION (D5 applied exactly, verbatim rule): Danger = ANY unpaid past month (not just previous month); Completed overrides Danger when months paid >= tenure; zero-value = unpaid preserved
OUTPUT: refreshed status for the bond (Danger | On-going | Completed)
ERRORS: ledger change not committed or status engine failure -> raise named error ERR-status-recompute naming the bond; surface via AF-30, never a stale status served as if fresh
1. Preconditions: the ledger change from AF-10 (insert) or AF-11 (correct/void) is committed; otherwise raise the named error.
2. Re-read the bond's ledger rows fresh from the database (no in-memory cache).
3. Recompute status with AF-14 applying the D5 rule exactly: ANY unpaid past month yields Danger; months paid >= tenure yields Completed and overrides Danger; amount 0 counts as unpaid.
4. Removing or zeroing an older past-month payment flips an On-going bond to Danger on the next read.
5. A bond already Completed stays Completed because Completed overrides Danger.
6. Return the recomputed status immediately; no file open, save or restart event is required for the new status to be visible (FR-20/FR-24), and the status is not written anywhere.
entries.complexity_note: single re-read plus O(tenure) D5 scan
edge_cases: void an old past-month payment -> On-going becomes Danger on next read
zero out an old payment row -> same Danger flip (zero = unpaid)
payment added that reaches full tenure -> Completed even if earlier gaps existed
recompute triggered before commit -> named error, no half-updated status

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: all bonds, payment_ledger table, current month
INPUT ASSERTION (D5 applied exactly, verbatim rule): Danger = ANY unpaid past month (not just previous month); Completed overrides Danger when months paid >= tenure; zero-value = unpaid preserved
OUTPUT: status per bond for the full portfolio (Danger | On-going | Completed each)
ERRORS: any single bond failing status computation -> collect the named error with the bond id and abort the sweep (or surface per-bond via AF-30); bonds are never silently skipped (ERR-01)
1. Triggers: application startup, import commit completed (AF-09), bulk ledger maintenance.
2. SELECT every bond from bonds; iterate all of them with no filtering and no legacy window cutoff.
3. For each bond, run AF-14 over its ledger rows under the D5 rule exactly: ANY unpaid past month yields Danger; months paid >= tenure yields Completed and overrides Danger; zero counts as unpaid.
4. Bonds beyond any legacy window (e.g. Feb-2031+ starters) are evaluated by the same rules, never silently skipped.
5. Build the in-memory map bond id -> status; do not write any status snapshot table or status column — results are used on view only.
6. If a bond fails to compute, raise the named error naming that bond; a partial sweep is never reported as complete.
entries.complexity_note: O(bonds x tenure) — one D5 scan per bond
edge_cases: portfolio with a Feb-2031+ starter -> still evaluated and listed
bond with no ledger rows at all -> On-going or Danger by D5 window rules, computed not skipped
one bond's metadata corrupt -> named error surfaced, sweep not silently truncated
no status snapshot persisted -> repeated sweeps are idempotent reads

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: bonds table, current D5 statuses (AF-14/AF-16)
OUTPUT: counts — total, danger, ongoing, completed
ERRORS: status computation failure for any bond -> raise named error ERR-query-counts; surface via AF-30, never a silent 0 count
1. Load the current D5 status for every bond (compute live via AF-16, no stored snapshot read).
2. total = number of bonds in the table.
3. danger = count of bonds whose status is Danger; ongoing = count of On-going; completed = count of Completed.
4. Assert danger + ongoing + completed = total; a mismatch raises the named error (a status could not be computed).
5. Return the four counts as a pure query result; nothing is stored or cached between requests.
entries.complexity_note: single query over bonds plus live status computation
edge_cases: empty portfolio -> all counts 0, legitimate query result
status computation error -> named error, never a partial count presented as final
no stored snapshot -> counts always reflect the latest ledger state

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: bonds table, payment_ledger table
OUTPUT: Total Investment, Total Till Return, Total Balance
ERRORS: underlying query failure -> raise named error ERR-query-summary-amounts; surface via AF-30, never a silent 0 on failure
1. total_investment = SUM(bonds.principle_tl).
2. total_till_return = SUM(payment_ledger.amount) where paid flag is true and amount > 0.
3. total_balance = total_till_return - SUM(bonds.maturity_amount) (Till Return minus Maturity Amount).
4. Each figure equals the query result over current data — no cached snapshot, no stored total column (DATA-05).
5. Return the three figures for the dashboard; a query error surfaces visibly via AF-30 rather than rendering zeros.
entries.complexity_note: three aggregate queries (single query class)
edge_cases: ledger updated a moment ago -> next request reflects it (live query)
empty tables -> genuine zeros only if the query succeeded
query exception -> visible named error, not a silent 0 (ERR-03)

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: payment_ledger table, current calendar month
OUTPUT: this-month total, or an explicit unresolvable-month message
ERRORS: current month cannot be resolved -> produce an explicit message stating the failure (ERR-03); never a silent 0; ledger query failure -> raise named error via AF-30
1. Resolve the current calendar month to YYYY-MM from the system clock.
2. If resolution fails (clock error, timezone failure, unparseable result), return the explicit message 'current month could not be resolved' — never a silent 0.
3. SELECT SUM(payment_ledger.amount) for rows with month = resolved month AND paid flag true AND amount > 0.
4. If no rows match, the total is 0 because the query succeeded and genuinely found nothing — distinct from step 2's failure message.
5. Return the total (or the message) as a live query result; nothing is stored.
entries.complexity_note: single query on the current month
edge_cases: clock or month resolution failure -> explicit message, never silent 0 (ERR-03)
current month with no payments yet -> genuine 0 from a successful query
mid-month payment edit -> next request reflects it immediately

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: payment_ledger table, derived month window
OUTPUT: month/total rows for the full history range, one row per month, future months shown as 0
ERRORS: window derivation failure or query failure -> raise named error ERR-query-history; surface via AF-30, never a silently truncated table
1. Derive the month window at runtime: earliest and latest month observed across ledger rows and bond due windows (the real workbook span is 83 months, 2025-09..2032-07) — no hardcoded Sep-2025..Feb-2027 header sequence and no window limit (FR-18).
2. Enumerate every month in the derived window continuously with no gaps.
3. For each month, total = SUM(payment_ledger.amount) for rows in that month with paid flag true and amount > 0.
4. Months with no ledger rows, including future months, render as 0 (query succeeded, nothing recorded).
5. Return the month/total rows; the current calendar month row carries a highlight marker for the view (R8 behavior), styling only, no data change.
6. A simulated current month beyond Feb-2027 still yields continuous rows with no missing months.
entries.complexity_note: one aggregate query plus O(window) row assembly
edge_cases: current month beyond Feb-2027 -> window extends, no clamp
months with zero payments -> present as 0 rows, not omitted
ledger empty -> empty or derived-from-bonds window reported explicitly, not a truncated default
no hardcoded header list anywhere in this function

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: bonds table, current D5 statuses (AF-14/AF-16)
OUTPUT: ordered bond rows with status and color key (red=Danger, orange=On-going, green=Completed)
ERRORS: status computation failure for any bond -> raise named error naming the bond via AF-30; no bond may be silently skipped (ERR-01)
1. Load the current D5 status for every bond (live, no stored snapshot).
2. Include ALL bonds in the output, including Feb-2031+ starters — skipping a bond is forbidden.
3. Order rows by status group: Danger first, then On-going, then Completed; within a group keep a stable secondary order (e.g. company name).
4. Attach the display color key per row: Danger -> red, On-going -> orange, Completed -> green.
5. Return the ordered rows as a pure query result for the view.
entries.complexity_note: single query plus O(n log n) status grouping sort
edge_cases: bond with no past due months -> On-going group, still listed
all bonds Completed -> single group, order preserved
one bond fails status computation -> named error, never a silently shortened list

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: HTTP GET dashboard request
OUTPUT: server-rendered dashboard HTML with live figures
ERRORS: any dashboard query failure -> render the visible error page naming the failed operation via AF-30; never render default zeros or an empty-success page for a failed query (FR-21)
1. On every request, execute the dashboard queries fresh: summary counts (AF-17), summary amounts (AF-18), this-month returns (AF-19), monthly history (AF-20), status overview (AF-21).
2. There is no open/save event and no stored snapshot: freshness comes from querying on every request.
3. If the current month cannot be resolved, render the explicit message from AF-19, not a silent 0.
4. Render the server-side HTML template with the returned figures and color keys.
5. Any query exception is converted by AF-30 into a visible error page naming the operation; a failed query never renders as a completed page with zeros.
6. Respond with status 200 and the rendered HTML on success; respond with an explicit error body naming the failed operation on failure.
entries.complexity_note: five queries per request, O(portfolio size) per request
edge_cases: reload right after a payment edit -> updated figures with no open/save/restart
one query fails mid-request -> visible error page, not partial zeros
unresolvable current month -> explicit message rendered
no cached dashboard snapshot exists anywhere

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: launch command, project folder
OUTPUT: running local Flask server, browser tab showing the dashboard
ERRORS: Python missing, port unavailable, schema missing, or import failure at startup -> raise named error ERR-launch naming the failing precondition; surface visibly, never a silent no-op (FR-21)
1. Preconditions: Python interpreter present, project folder present and readable, browser available.
2. Run the single documented launch command from the project root.
3. Ensure the schema exists (AF-01) before serving; if it is absent, run schema init or report the named precondition failure.
4. Bind the Flask server to 127.0.0.1 only — localhost, no outbound network exposure.
5. Serve plain server-rendered HTML with no build step, no npm and no bundler.
6. Open or point the browser at the dashboard URL; a working dashboard must be reachable within 60 seconds on a clean machine (NFR-4).
7. Any startup failure prints a visible message naming the failed step (port in use, missing dependency, unreadable database) instead of exiting silently.
entries.complexity_note: startup path, constant work
edge_cases: port already in use -> visible named error with the port, not a silent exit
database file absent -> schema init or named precondition error
dependency (Flask/openpyxl) missing -> visible named error naming the package

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: bond metadata (start month, tenure), payment_ledger rows per bond, current D5 statuses, current month
OUTPUT: server-rendered month-grid HTML with dynamic columns and color classes
ERRORS: status or ledger query failure -> raise named error ERR-render-grid via AF-30; never render a partially colored grid as if complete
1. Derive the month window at render time per bond: from the bond's start month through max(current month, start + tenure - 1) — no hardcoded Sep-2025..Feb-2027 headers and no Jan-2031 limit (FR-18/FR-19).
2. Enumerate month columns continuously with no missing months and no schema change (months are rows, columns are display only).
3. For each bond row, look up its ledger entries by (bond id, month).
4. Color cells: paid (paid flag true and amount > 0) -> green; unpaid due month (past or current, no row or amount 0) -> light red; not yet due future month -> neutral.
5. Render the status cell with red/orange/green for Danger/On-going/Completed from the live D5 status (AF-14).
6. A bond starting Feb-2031 or later renders all its month rows with correct coloring — no silent skip (ERR-01).
7. Any query failure raises the named error; the error page is rendered via AF-30 instead of a misleading empty grid.
entries.complexity_note: O(bonds x months) render assembly
edge_cases: bond starting Feb-2031+ -> full grid rendered, no clamp
zero-amount cell -> renders as unpaid (light red), not paid green
bond with tenure extending past current month -> future columns neutral, continuous
query failure -> visible error, not an empty-but-successful grid

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: POST payment form (bond id, month, amount)
OUTPUT: ledger row inserted or corrected (AF-10/AF-11), recomputed status (AF-15), redirect to the month grid
ERRORS: bond missing, month unparseable, amount non-numeric, or ledger write failure -> return a visible error message naming the failed operation via AF-30; never accept the edit silently or redirect as if it succeeded
1. Validate the form: bond id resolves, month parses to YYYY-MM, amount is numeric (0 allowed and stored as unpaid).
2. If a ledger row already exists for (bond_id, month), apply a correction through AF-11; otherwise insert through AF-10.
3. After the ledger change commits, recompute the bond's status immediately under D5 with AF-15 — no open/save event is required (FR-20/FR-24).
4. On any validation or write failure, respond with a visible message naming the failed operation; do not redirect as success.
5. On success, redirect back to the month grid view so the next render shows the updated cell color and the recomputed status color.
6. The handler never writes a status value; status stays computed at view time.
entries.complexity_note: single insert or update plus one status recompute
edge_cases: edit an older past-month payment to 0 -> row stored with 0, status flips to Danger on next read
edit that completes the tenure -> Completed, overriding any earlier gaps
duplicate submit of the same (bond, month) -> correction path, no duplicate row
invalid month string -> visible validation error, no silent drop

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: dataset identifier (view), rows and headers currently displayed for that view
OUTPUT: UTF-8 CSV file download
ERRORS: unknown dataset id, missing rows, or encoding failure -> raise named error ERR-export-view naming the dataset; surface via AF-30, never an empty file offered as a successful export
1. Resolve the dataset id to the view's currently displayed rows and headers — export reads the SAME rows the screen shows, never a different source.
2. If the view is unknown or its rows are unavailable, raise the named error instead of exporting an empty file.
3. Serialize with RFC-4180-ish quoting: fields containing comma, double quote or line breaks are wrapped in double quotes, embedded double quotes are doubled (""), records separated by CRLF, header row first.
4. Encode the output as UTF-8 (with BOM optional for spreadsheet compatibility) so rupee amounts parse as plain values with no encoding errors.
5. Emit a CSV download only — no xlsx export is produced (D4: CSV replaces xlsx entirely).
6. Any serialization failure raises the named error; a partially written file is not offered as success.
entries.complexity_note: O(rows x columns) serialization of the displayed set
edge_cases: value contains comma or quote -> RFC-4180 quoting applied
rupee or non-ASCII characters -> UTF-8 encoding, no mojibake in spreadsheet apps
unknown dataset id -> named error, not an empty CSV
view currently showing zero rows -> export of headers-only CSV is allowed only when the view itself rendered successfully

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: payment_ledger table (all rows)
OUTPUT: UTF-8 CSV file of the full ledger
ERRORS: ledger query failure or encoding failure -> raise named error ERR-export-ledger; surface via AF-30, never an empty or partial file reported as complete
1. SELECT every payment_ledger row ordered by bond id then month, carrying bond ref, month, amount, paid flag.
2. If the query fails, raise the named error; an empty ledger exports a headers-only CSV only when the query genuinely returned zero rows.
3. Serialize with RFC-4180-ish quoting (quote fields with commas/quotes/newlines, double embedded quotes, CRLF record separators).
4. Encode UTF-8; amounts export as plain numeric values with no currency symbols that would break parsing.
5. The export contents must match a direct ledger query row-for-row; any mismatch is an error, not a warning to ignore.
6. Emit the CSV download; no xlsx output (D4).
entries.complexity_note: O(all ledger rows) single query plus serialization
edge_cases: ledger with zero rows -> headers-only CSV from a successful query
amount 0 rows -> exported verbatim with paid flag false
query failure -> named error, not an empty file

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: full set of bond ISIN values (extracted set or bonds table)
OUTPUT: list of duplicated ISIN values with all their occurrences
ERRORS: input set unavailable -> raise named error ERR-duplicate-check; the check itself never swallows a found duplicate (FR-21)
1. Take the COMPLETE bond set — never a partial row range (a scan limited to the first N rows is forbidden).
2. Group entries by ISIN value; any group with more than one entry is a duplicate.
3. For each duplicated ISIN, record the value and EVERY occurrence with its row/index (e.g. row 2 and row 40 of 40 bonds both flagged).
4. Return the duplicate list; an empty list means the full set was scanned and found clean.
5. Callers (AF-07 import validation, web forms, periodic checks) treat a non-empty result as a hard failure to surface, never as a warning to ignore.
entries.complexity_note: single pass, O(n) grouping over the full set
edge_cases: duplicate far down the set (row 40 of 40) -> caught, full-set scan
same ISIN twice with different formatting -> normalized comparison before grouping, both occurrences reported
empty input set -> empty result, distinct from a scan error

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: code paths reading or writing bond/ledger fields, schema key registry
OUTPUT: pass/fail decoupling verdict, plus a list of any header-string or fixed-position couplings found
ERRORS: any coupling found -> fail the verdict with the offending path listed; a failing gate blocks the change (FR-21), never a warning-only pass
1. Load the schema key registry for bonds and payment_ledger (the stable field names).
2. Scan the given code paths for field access patterns: any keying on workbook header text (e.g. reading by the literal string 'Company Name') or on fixed column numbers (e.g. column 4, column 14) is a coupling.
3. Import column mapping (AF-03) must use keyword detection resolved to schema keys — that is the allowed pattern; raw header strings as persistent keys are not.
4. List every coupling found with its file and line.
5. Renaming a display label (e.g. Staus -> Status) must change no query, no status rule and no import behavior — verify by re-running the gate after such a rename; a behavior change means a coupling exists and the gate fails.
6. Verdict: pass only when zero couplings are found; otherwise fail with the list.
entries.complexity_note: static scan over registered code paths
edge_cases: display label renamed -> gate still passes, no logic change
keyword detection in AF-03 -> allowed (maps to schema keys), not counted as coupling
hard-coded month column index in a query -> flagged as coupling, gate fails

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: operation name, raised exception or failure condition
OUTPUT: visible error message or error page naming the failed operation
ERRORS: this function IS the error path — any failure entering here must produce a user-visible message naming the operation; swallowing, default zeros, empty success or ignore-and-continue fallbacks are forbidden (FR-21, replaces VBA On Error Resume Next)
1. Wrap each operation (import step, route handler, query, export) so its failures funnel into this handler with the operation name.
2. Catch the exception or failure condition; do NOT suppress it and do NOT substitute a default success value.
3. Compose a message that names the failed operation and the underlying reason (e.g. 'reconciliation failed: Total Till Return computed 56227.88 vs baseline 111638.57').
4. For web routes, render the error page with that message; for the import pipeline, abort the whole run and print the failures.
5. Never present default zeros, an empty result or an ignore-and-continue as a completed operation; a partial import is never reported as success (ERR-05).
6. Every induced failure (unreadable XLSM, missing sheet, reconciliation break, query error, export error, unresolvable current month) must produce a visible message — this is the verification obligation of FR-21.
entries.complexity_note: constant work per failure; gate function
edge_cases: unreadable XLSM -> visible message naming open-workbook, no silent empty import
missing sheet -> visible message naming the sheet lookup
reconciliation break -> visible L1 message with computed vs baseline figures
query error on a route -> visible error page, never a page of zeros
unresolvable current month -> explicit message, never silent 0 (ERR-03)

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: home_plan table rows (imported via AF-05/AF-09)
OUTPUT: server-rendered Home Plan HTML listing all 84 months plus totals
ERRORS: home_plan table missing or query failure -> raise named error ERR-render-homeplan via AF-30; never render a truncated schedule as if complete
1. SELECT all home_plan rows ordered by month_index.
2. Verify the rows cover month_index 1..84 contiguously; a gap raises the named error naming the missing index.
3. Render each row with saving, rate, per-year interest, countdown and remaining interest exactly from stored values — no recomputation that could drift from the imported Excel values (ERR-06 verbatim preservation).
4. Ensure irregular savings 39588, 10063 and 0 appear in their original month positions exactly as stored.
5. Append the stored schedule totals (Per Month / Per Year / TL summary rows) at the end of the table.
6. Any query or completeness failure produces the visible error page via AF-30, not a partial schedule.
entries.complexity_note: single query over 84 rows
edge_cases: irregular savings values 39588, 10063, 0 -> verbatim in original positions
saving 0 is a stored value, rendered as 0, not treated as missing
fewer than 84 rows in the table -> named error, no silent truncation
formula-derived cells -> rendered from imported cached values, not re-derived

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: watch-list inputs per bond (AF-06)
OUTPUT: analytics rows — face value, principle, T.L.P, discount, per-month, 10% TDS, 12-month total, qty, TL principle
ERRORS: missing required input for a bond or computation failure -> raise named error ERR-watch-analytics naming the bond and field via AF-30; never substitute a default 0 for a missing input
1. For each bond's watch-list inputs, compute on view: discount from the discount inputs, 10% TDS = discount x 0.10, per-month figures, qty TL and the 12-month totals, reproducing the Excel watch-list formulas over the same inputs (DATA-04).
2. Read inputs from the imported watch-list records; if a required input is absent for a bond, raise the named error naming the field.
3. Compare spot-checks against the Excel watch-list outputs for the same bond; a mismatch is reported, not silently tolerated.
4. Return computed analytics rows only — analytics are never persisted as columns (computed on view).
5. Any computation exception surfaces visibly via AF-30; no silent 0 substitution.
entries.complexity_note: O(bonds) arithmetic, pure compute
edge_cases: missing discount input -> named error for that bond, not a default 0
zero discount -> legitimate computed 0 from present inputs
results differ from Excel formulas -> reported as a mismatch, not silently accepted

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: bonds with principal amounts, current D5 statuses
OUTPUT: available principal to reinvest, deduction breakdown excluding Completed bonds
ERRORS: status computation failure or query failure -> raise named error ERR-reinvestment via AF-30; never report a partial free-up figure as final
1. Load current D5 status for every bond (AF-14/AF-16, live).
2. available = SUM(bonds.principle_tl) over bonds whose status is Completed — a Completed bond's full principal is reported as available to reinvest.
3. Apply duplicate-deduction rules ONLY to bonds whose status is On-going or Danger: sum their principals (and any applicable duplicate deductions) as the deduction total.
4. A Completed bond is never deducted — exclude it from the deduction breakdown entirely so its principal is never deducted twice (FR-17).
5. Return the available figure and the deduction breakdown grouped by status.
6. Any failure surfaces visibly via AF-30; a figure computed over a partial status set is never returned as final.
entries.complexity_note: O(bonds) grouping over live statuses
edge_cases: all bonds Completed -> full principal available, zero deductions
mix of statuses -> Completed principal fully available, deductions only from On-going/Danger
a Completed bond with historical gaps -> still Completed (D5), still fully available, never deducted
status computation failure -> named error, no partial total

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: bond record including the discount column
OUTPUT: discount amount displayed on the bond detail view
ERRORS: bonds.discount column missing or bond not found -> raise named error ERR-bond-discount naming the bond via AF-30; never display a blank or default 0 as if the record were complete
1. Load the bond record by id from bonds, including the discount field.
2. If the bond is absent or the discount column is missing from the schema, raise the named error.
3. The discount value comes directly from the bond record — it is a stored input, not a derived cache.
4. Display the discount amount alongside the other master fields on the bond detail view (Phase 4).
5. If the bond has no recorded discount (null), display it as not recorded; do not fabricate 0 as a computed value.
entries.complexity_note: single row read (single query)
edge_cases: discount null -> displayed as not recorded, not a fake 0
discount 0 stored -> displayed as 0, a real recorded value
bond id not found -> named error via AF-30

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: payout amount, TDS rate (10%)
OUTPUT: TDS amount, net payout amount
ERRORS: payout amount missing or non-numeric, or rate outside (0,1] -> raise named error ERR-tds-compute via AF-30; never return a silent 0 TDS on failure
1. Validate the payout amount is numeric and non-negative; otherwise raise the named error.
2. Validate the TDS rate (default 0.10 per the workbook watch-list formula) is greater than 0 and at most 1.
3. tds_amount = payout_amount x rate.
4. net_payout = payout_amount - tds_amount.
5. Check: a due payout of 10000 at 10% TDS yields TDS 1000 and net 9000.
6. Return both figures computed per payout — TDS is never stored (computed at render time).
entries.complexity_note: constant arithmetic per payout
edge_cases: payout 10000 at 10% -> TDS 1000, net 9000
payout 0 -> TDS 0 and net 0 from a valid computation, not an error
non-numeric payout -> named error, not a silent 0
rate 0 or negative -> named error (invalid configuration), not a free pass

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: interest_start_month, tenure_months, payment_type (monthly|quarterly|yearly)
OUTPUT: list of due months across the tenure
ERRORS: unparseable start month, tenure <= 0, or unknown payment type -> raise named error ERR-due-dates naming the bad field via AF-30; never fall back to monthly silently
1. Parse interest_start_month to YYYY-MM; on failure raise the named error.
2. Validate tenure_months is a positive integer and payment_type is one of monthly, quarterly, yearly; an unknown type raises the named error (never defaults to monthly).
3. Generate candidate months start, start+1, ... through start + tenure - 1 (inclusive).
4. Filter by cycle: monthly -> every month; quarterly -> months where the offset from start is divisible by 3 (start Sep-2025 yields Sep-2025, Dec-2025, Mar-2026, ... through the tenure); yearly -> offsets divisible by 12 (exactly one due date per year of the tenure).
5. Return the due months sorted ascending; the ledger stays month-row based — the cycle only determines which months are due.
entries.complexity_note: O(tenure) generation
edge_cases: quarterly bond starting Sep-2025 -> Sep-2025, Dec-2025, Mar-2026, ... not every month
yearly bond -> exactly one due date per year of the tenure
monthly bond -> every month of the tenure
tenure not divisible by the cycle -> only whole cycle steps inside the tenure are due
unknown payment type -> named error, never a silent monthly fallback

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: bonds table, payment_ledger table, current D5 statuses
OUTPUT: P&L figure, ongoing TL value
ERRORS: query or status failure -> raise named error ERR-dashboard-pnl via AF-30; never render default zeros for a failed computation
1. Load current D5 statuses for all bonds (AF-14/AF-16).
2. Compute Total Till Return = SUM(payment_ledger.amount) over paid rows (amount > 0), and Total Investment = SUM(bonds.principle_tl), using AF-13/AF-18 query logic.
3. pnl = Total Till Return - Total Investment (Stage-7 PROPOSED P&L definition for the dashboard, Phase 4 - AWAITING OWNER CONFIRMATION: no baseline defines P&L; maturity-minus-investment is an equally valid alternative; record as open point before Phase 4 implementation).
4. ongoing_tl = SUM(bonds.principle_tl) over bonds whose status is On-going (the ongoing bond total TL value).
5. Return both figures as live query results over current ledger and bond data — no cached snapshot, matching the dashboard freshness model.
6. Any underlying failure surfaces visibly via AF-30; zeros appear only when the computation genuinely returns them.
entries.complexity_note: two aggregate queries plus status grouping
edge_cases: portfolio all Completed -> ongoing_tl is 0 from a successful computation
ledger edited just before the request -> figures reflect the edit on the next request
status computation failure -> named error, not zeros rendered as success
empty portfolio -> genuine zeros only if queries succeed
P&L definition not yet confirmed by owner (Stage-7 proposal only) - Phase 4 must not implement until confirmed
